page.title: B-trees
page.desc: Wide, shallow balanced trees (Bayer and McCreight, 1972) designed for storage that reads in blocks; the index structure in most databases and many filesystems.
page.intro: Wide, shallow balanced trees (Bayer and McCreight, 1972) designed for storage that reads in blocks; the index structure in most databases and many filesystems.

synapses.text: Each node fills a page and holds hundreds of keys, so a lookup touches only a handful of pages even for billions of rows.
Both store tables and indexes as B-tree variants; the SQLite file format documentation describes its B+-tree pages in detail.

parent.title: Trees
parent.desc: Hierarchical structures of nodes and children. Binary search trees give ordered lookup, B-trees power databases and filesystems, tries index strings by prefix.
